messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty PD-78241 fired — high latency p99 (eu-west) on inference-hotpath. 3m above SLO. Trigger: tokenization queue depth + KV eviction spike. Please ACK and investigate.

tj: Acked. I'm taking primary. @oliver can you check KV eviction and hotkeys? I'll look at recent deploys and autoscaler behavior.

oliver: Looking. KV eviction spiked ~2.8x around 12:03 UTC. Hotkey pattern on /embed route from a single customer shard. No error rate increase.

alex: Noted. There was a model-slicing deploy ~15m ago in eu-west (deploy-bot shows job 4627). Deploy completed cleanly. Correlating traces now.

deploy-bot: deploy job 4627 (model-slicer v2.4) completed at 12:00:41 UTC to eu-west pool.

maya: Quick customer check — support ticket #4452 shows reported slowness for one enterprise customer hitting embeddings-heavy paths. They report response times ~3-6s. No 5xxs.

oliver: Hotkey + increased tokenization backlog causing tail latency. Starting temporary reroute of the offending shard to fallback pool (eu-west-fallback). Command: `reroute shard shard-17 -> eu-west-fallback` — executing.

tj: Also lowering batch_size on eu-west inference nodes to reduce queueing. Patch: batch_size 32 -> 16. I'm applying via config rollout now: `cfgctl set inference.batch_size=16 --subset=eu-west`

alex: Running quick latency probe: `curl -s https://metrics.internal/api/series?p=tail_latency&region=eu-west` returns summary: p95 420ms -> 260ms after initial reroute start, p99 still ~1.8s.

oliver: Reroute finished. Confirming shard-17 traffic diverted. KV eviction rate dropping. Watching warmup for eu-west-fallback.

tj: Good. I'm enabling prefix/KV caching for high-token flows as a temporary measure: `feature-toggle enable kv-prefix-cache --region=eu-west`.

maya: Customer impact note: affected customer incidents opened, engineering triage status updated in support ticket. No SLA credits yet; monitoring.

oliver: p95 trending down to 230ms, p99 down from 1.9s to 650ms after reroute + batch change. Still above SLO target of 500ms p99 but improving.

incident-bot: Pager escalated to level-2 — auto-escalation at +5m (PD-78241 -> PD-78241-L2).

alex: Traces indicate a small regression in tokenization latency from v2.4 under high-concurrency tiny-requests. I'll prepare a rollback candidate if p99 doesn't stabilize in 10m.

tj: Agreed. If p99 stays >700ms after 10m we'll roll back model-slicer to v2.3 for eu-west. For now continue observation.

oliver: Spinning up two extra fallback workers to aid warmup: `kubectl scale deployment inference-fallback --replicas=4 -n eu-west`.

maya: Noted — I've posted a short customer update to the support ticket and flagged SRE engagement.

tj: p95 stable, p99 ~430ms now. Eviction continued to drop. I'm going to start a short bridge for 30m in case of reflare. Handing active incident to morning oncall @lara for follow-up and postmortem prep. Lara, please take ownership for next steps: KV warmup, deploy rollback decision if needed, and write a short postmortem if total SLO burn exceeds 15m.

lara: Taking handoff, ack. I'll keep the bridge open and collect artifacts.

oliver: TL;DR mitigation applied: reroute hotkey shard -> fallback, reduce batch_size, enable prefix cache, scale fallback workers. Immediate customer impact reduced.

tj: Thanks — :thumbsup: — I'll close the pager if things stay stable for the next 15m.

incident-bot: Pager PD-78241 acknowledged by tj; last alert at 12:07 UTC.

lara: I'll follow up with a brief incident note and coordinate postmortem. If anything re-triggers ping me on this thread.

alex: Saving relevant traces and metrics to the incident folder: `/incidents/2026-03-17/pd-78241/` — will attach dive links.

tj: Closing bridge in 20m unless we see a spike. Good coordination, team.

lara: Copy. I'll file the postmortem template and assign action items.
